question.text: GAAR (General Anti-Avoidance Rules, effective April 1, 2017) and the Multilateral Instrument (MLI, 2018 under BEPS) have together moved India's approach to offshore fund structures from:

answer.text: Pure territorial taxation to pure residence-based taxation

explanation.text: The Logic: Previously, Indian tax authorities often accepted the LEGAL form of an offshore structure (Mauritius SPV, for example) at face value. Post-GAAR and MLI-BEPS, they apply a 'substance over form' test — they look at where the real commercial substance lies. Hollow Mauritius SPVs with no local substance are challenged. The Trap: Options A, C, D are reversed or fabricated. The BEPS project's entire thrust is 'substance over form' to prevent base erosion. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C/XIX-D both test GAAR/MLI. XIX-E applies the same framework to Cat III offshore structures. Manager's Pro-Tip: When you set up an offshore feeder, document real substance: local directors, board meetings in-jurisdiction, local service providers. A paper-only SPV is GAAR-challenge bait in any audit.
